 Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico at WWE Survivor Series 2026
 Graham GSM Matthews Nov 16, 2026 
 The classic Survivor Series tag team elimination match returning at WWE Survivor Series 2026 after a five-year absence gives fans good reason to rejoice.
 The bout was announced as Team USA vs. Team Mexico, with the two teams featuring stars from SmackDown, Raw and AAA. Even with nothing currently at stake, it should be a fun showcase for 10 top talents who might otherwise miss out on the November 28 card. 
 Immediately following Crown Jewel, it was determined that Cody Rhodes would lead Team USA while Rey Mysterio would serve as the captain for Team Mexico. It was then confirmed that CM Punk and Je'Von Evans would join Rhodes, with Penta and Rey Fenix being added to Mysterio's squad.
 That leaves two spots open on each all-star team, and any number of names could realistically fill them. AAA has plenty of people available for Team Mexico to choose from, and there are enough directionless Superstars on the red and blue brands right now that Team USA has no shortage of intriguing options.
 These are the most likely possibilities for the final members of Team USA and Team Mexico at Survivor Series.
 Team USA: Seth Rollins
 1 of 6 WWE/WWE via Getty Images 
 Seth Rollins has been conspicuous by his absence on WWE TV since SummerSlam. Seeing as how he isn't currently dealing with a major injury, however, he should be back on Raw relatively soon.
 Interestingly, there's no one obvious path for him upon his return. He wrapped up his rivalry with Roman Reigns and shouldn't be pursuing the World Heavyweight Championship again anytime soon, so he'll essentially be starting from scratch.
 In that case, he would be a fine fit for Team USA, simply so he can be brought back into the mix on Monday nights with a bang and work alongside some of Raw and SmackDown's biggest and brightest stars.
 There was a point in time when he and Cody Rhodes were allies, and it would be a surreal sight for him to join forces with Punk after how long they spent at odds with each other. Whoever eliminates him (or helps him get eliminated for that matter) could be his next rival coming out of the event.
 It was at the Thanksgiving week classic that Rollins debuted as part of The Shield 14 years ago, so it'd be only appropriate for him to be a part of the show this year.
 Team Mexico: El Grande Americano
 2 of 6 Lucha Libre AAA/WWE via Getty Images 
 El Grande Americano has been the biggest breakout star in AAA over the last year, going from being a comedy character on Raw to being the most beloved babyface on the entire AAA roster.
 He really started to hit his stride after besting Chad Gable's Americano in a Mask vs. Mask match back in May before finally winning the AAA Mega Championship in September. He's largely been kept exclusive to the AAA brand since then but came across like a total star when he popped up on Raw in Mexico soon after.
 Of course, the man portraying Americano, Ludwig Kaiser, wasn't actually born and raised in Mexico, but it wouldn't be too shocking of WWE to put him on Team Mexico, anyway. He has a close relationship with the captain Rey Mysterio in AAA and most fans would just be happy to see him.
 At the very least, it'd give AAA more exposure at Survivor Series since he remains the reigning Mega champ, and having him eliminate someone from Team USA would be a big boost to the brand.
 No one else from AAA at the moment feels like a big enough deal to take up one of the spots on Team Mexico, though someone like La Parka or Mini Vikingo would have way more to gain from being afforded that opportunity than Americano, who is a made man at this point.
 Team USA: Trick Williams
 3 of 6 WWE/WWE via Getty Images 
 It would be silly for Trick Williams to not at least be considered for a spot on Team USA given he's the United States champion. 
 Additionally, he's a star on the rise and has had an incredible rookie year. He's held the star-spangled prize on and off since WrestleMania 42 and has racked up wins over the likes of Sami Zayn, Baron Corbin and Carmelo Hayes.
 He has future world champion written all over him and thus it wouldn't be a stretch to see him challenging for a top title sometime in 2027. With that in mind, he should be a part of Team USA so he can benefit from teaming with massive stars in Cody Rhodes and CM Punk.
 Williams is likely headed for a feud with Damian Priest, but he can join Team USA while also continuing to defend his title against all comers. He recently failed to dethrone Zayn for the Undisputed WWE Championship and isn't doing anything else of note at the moment. 
 Williams being among the sole survivors would be huge for him.

 Bleacher Report 6h Team Mexico: Dragon Lee
 4 of 6 WWE/WWE via Getty Images 
 Dragon Lee is one of the most exciting wrestlers to watch in all of WWE. His booking has vastly improved from where it was a year ago, and he's now a regular on Raw and competing in meaningful matches. 
 Lee has come close to capturing the Intercontinental Championship on countless occasions this year but became the number one contender once again last Monday night. Regardless of when he gets his next shot at the strap, he can easily be added to Team Mexico at Survivor Series.
 With Rey Mysterio leading the team, Lee is a logical choice given how frequently they've teamed up this year. He'd obviously excel alongside him and The Lucha Brothers, as all of their aerial offense would make for a blast of a bout.
 It'd also be odd for every luchador on the main roster to be a part of it but not Lee, so one of the two vacancies really should go to him. It'd be another chance for him to showcase his skills as well as face a few people he's never squared off against before.
 A strong showing at Survivor Series would go a long way in ultimately elevating him on the card and earning him an eventual run with singles gold.
 Team USA: Chad Gable
 5 of 6 WWE/WWE via Getty Images 
 Chad Gable is right up there with Dragon Lee as one of Raw's MVPs in 2026 thanks to his consistently strong performances in the ring. He's also enjoying the greatest success of his career to date. 
 He held the Intercontinental Championship for only three months but had a memorable run in that time, delivering weekly bangers with the midcard of the red brand and making that title feel like the most coveted prize on Raw.
 He dropped the belt to Ethan Page earlier this year and subsequently fell short of becoming number one contender, so Gable is free to do virtually anything else going forward. Between that and Gable being a U.S. Olympian, it should be a no-brainer to get him on Team USA. 
 At the end of October, Gable went one-on-one with CM Punk for the first time ever and shockingly went over in clean fashion. Although it wasn't acknowledged on television, Punk can mention on Raw that he gained respect for Gable from that match before recruiting him to the team.
 Gable being a part of this stacked bout would serve as a nice culmination to the story he's had with all of WWE's luchadors this year.
 Team Mexico: Dominik Mysterio
 6 of 6 WWE/WWE via Getty Images 
 Dominik Mysterio was the very first one to attempt to throw his name into the hat as a member of either Team USA or Team Mexico. He was quickly denied by both Rey Mysterio and Cody Rhodes before being laid out. 
 Mysterio and Rhodes have had their fair share of issues with Dirty Dom in the past, so it made sense that they wouldn't allow him to join with such ease. That's also what makes him such a compelling candidate, specifically for Team Mexico.
 Despite showing zero signs of slowing down, Rey could be headed for in-ring retirement as soon as next year, and if so, he and Dom should team up at least one last time, albeit reluctantly. 
 Dom might be among the most despised stars in WWE today, but his accolades alone would make him a valuable asset to the team.
 He wrapped up a year-long run as AAA Mega champion two months ago, so he has a track record of being a draw for the AAA brand. He's been spinning his wheels ever since and forcing him to team with his father would ideally get something going for him.
 There's a strong possibility that weeks of begging and pleading to get on the team could lead to Dom getting eliminated almost immediately, but it would be a story worth telling in the coming weeks and get him back in the spotlight where he belongs.
